summary.text: Annette Death is Labor's candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian state election. She sat on Macedon Ranges Shire Council, serving as mayor in 2023-24, and her earlier career included policy work at St Vincent's Health. Raised in central Victoria, she lives in Riddells Creek and was the first in her family to attend university.

priorities.text: Regional health care, citing the free Virtual Emergency Department and the Cobaw Community Health Hub
Urgent care that working families in regional areas can reach when they need it

summary.text: Catherine Wilson is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a teacher who has lived in the Macedon Ranges for about two decades. She is active in the Australian Education Union and in Socialists in Schools, a rank-and-file group of educators.

priorities.text: Our public education system is in crisis.
Better pay for teachers and support staff, smaller classes and less paperwork
More public housing, paid for partly by higher taxes on short-stay rentals such as Airbnb
A universal, publicly run disability service in place of the for-profit NDIS market
Spending AUKUS submarine funds on health and education instead

His One Nation candidate page could not be read for this profile.

occupation.text: Mechanic; owner of a small transport business

summary.text: Dom Bonanno is running as an independent for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian election. He has been a Macedon Ranges Shire councillor since 2020, including a year as mayor, and has spent about 30 years working in information technology. He stood for Macedon as the Liberal candidate in 2022 and is now campaigning without a party, while on unpaid leave from council.

prior_roles.note: Re-elected in 2024; on unpaid leave from the role during his state campaign, according to his website.

previous_candidacies.note: His website says he was elected in 2020; no source gives the label he ran under.
His website says he was re-elected in 2024; no source gives the label he ran under.

priorities.text: I also oppose the proposed Clarkefield township.
I support scrapping the Emergency Services and Volunteers tax.
A Victorian version of Jack's Law, letting police scan for knives with handheld detectors
Long-term funding to repair regional roads rather than short-term patching
Cutting government waste and the cost of state debt while keeping frontline services

summary.text: Kate Kendall is the Liberal candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian election. She was mayor of Macedon Ranges Shire until she began her campaign for state parliament. Before that, according to the ABC's guide, she had a marketing career in Melbourne, set up a number of businesses and served as president of the local business group Business Kyneton.

summary.text: Marley McRae McLeod is the Greens candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian election, a second run for the seat after standing there for the party in 2022. They grew up in the Macedon area and work as a peer support worker with young people in a youth mental health service. Between those two state campaigns they were the Greens' running mate for deputy lord mayor of Melbourne in 2024 and the party's candidate for the federal seat of McEwen in 2025.

occupation.text: Peer support worker, youth mental health service

priorities.text: our politics needs integrity, our environment needs protection
Affordable mental health care and well-supported public schools
Responding to more extreme weather and the threat of bushfires in the district

summary.text: Michael Seton is an independent candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian election. A Woodend resident, he spent 35 years in superannuation and led two superannuation funds, AGEST Super and Military Super, as chief executive before retiring in 2024. He says he is funding his own campaign and taking no donations, and his platform centres on state debt and integrity in politics.

prior_roles.organisation: Australian Government Employees Superannuation Trust (AGEST Super)

priorities.text: I am not aligned to any political party, donor or lobbyist.
A legislated ceiling on state debt, set against Gross State Product or as a dollar cap
Opposes the battery energy storage system planned near Macedon
Truth in political advertising laws with real penalties
Stronger powers for IBAC

summary.text: Natalie Korinfsky is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Macedon at the 2026 Victorian state election. A social worker and youth worker from Kyneton, she worked for a decade in youth work at Macedon Ranges Shire Council and has supported schools across the Loddon Campaspe region. She holds a master's degree in social work and an arts degree majoring in nature tourism and psychology, and is president of a local football club, the Wedge-Tailed Eagles.

priorities.text: Banning greyhound racing and ending the use of 1080 poison
Stronger animal welfare laws
Better public services, including mental health, health care, education and affordable housing
Tighter limits on gambling advertising, especially where children see it
More openness and accountability in government
